privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.heading: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: This site is a civic-tech tool. We collect the bare minimum and do not profile people for commercial purposes.

sections.title: Controller
sections.body: The Substrato project is curated by Relatronica, an independent non-profit initiative for speculative design, civic tech, and knowledge mapping.

sections.title: Data processed
sections.body: As a rule we do not ask for accounts or personal details. We may process: IP address and technical hosting logs (for security and operation); local preferences on your device (for example if you have already closed the welcome message); messages you send us voluntarily (reports, press inquiries).

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
sections.body: We do not use profiling or advertising cookies. We may use the browser's localStorage to remember interface choices (e.g. closing the welcome modal). You can clear it from your browser settings.

sections.title: Third parties
sections.body: The map loads tiles and libraries from third-party services (for example basemap and CDN). Place search sends the query to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Those providers may receive technical network requests (IP, user agent, search text) under their own notices. Links to external platforms (donations, social, GitHub) are under those services' control.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
sections.body: We process data to run the site, prevent abuse, respond to requests, and improve the public dataset. Legal basis: legitimate interest in operating a non-profit information tool and, for messages you send us, pre-contractual measures / contact at your request.

sections.title: Rights
sections.body: You may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction, or objection where applicable, and lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority. To exercise your rights, write to the privacy address listed on this page.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.heading: Terms of use
terms.lead: By using the site you accept these conditions. They are written to protect the community and clarify the limits of the data.

sections.title: Nature of the project
sections.body: The tool is informational, independent, and non-profit. It is not a commercial service, does not constitute legal, technical, or investment advice, and does not represent the positions of mapped companies.

sections.title: Incomplete or estimated data
sections.body: The dataset is evolving: it may be incomplete, delayed, inferred, or wrong. We prefer to declare sources and certainty levels rather than pretend completeness. Always verify primary sources before public or journalistic decisions.

sections.title: Permitted use
sections.body: You may explore, cite, and share the project, naming the project, URL, and date of access. Use for research, teaching, journalism, and advocacy is encouraged.

sections.title: Prohibited use
sections.body: You may not present the data as official or exhaustive; remove attributions; use the site for harassment, abusive profiling of people, or unlawful activity. Third-party datasets remain subject to their licenses (e.g. ODbL, CC BY).

sections.title: Liability
sections.body: To the extent permitted by law, Relatronica and the curators are not liable for damages arising from use of, or inability to use, the site or datasets. Report errors to us: they help the whole community.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We may update terms, interface, and data without notice. The date at the top of the page marks the last substantive revision of this text.

press.title: Press
press.heading: Press contacts
press.lead: For interviews, deeper coverage, quotes, or materials about the project, write to us. We reply in Italian or English.
press.body: Substrato is a civic map of the physical infrastructure of cloud and AI (data centers, energy, raw materials, connections), curated by Relatronica.
bullets: Angle and context for the project (civic tech, non-profit, Italy/Europe focus)
Clarifications on methodology, sources, and dataset limits

A link to Relatronica for other knowledge-mapping projects
press.how_body: Write with a clear subject (e.g. «Interview request — outlet name»), editorial deadline, and a link to the piece if it is already online.

report.title: Report
report.heading: Report data or an error
report.lead: The map improves with the community. Report missing sites, wrong coordinates, better sources, or notes on labor and territorial impact.
report.intro: Open a GitHub issue (preferred: it stays public and traceable) or write to the privacy/contacts address if you do not use GitHub. Always include: site name, approximate location, what looks wrong, and a source if you have one.

cards.title: Error or update
cards.body: A point out of place, closed, renamed, or an implausible connection.

cards.title: Missing site
cards.body: A relevant data center, plant, or node absent from the map.

cards.title: Source or methodology
cards.body: A proposal for an open source, license, or documentation improvement.

report.note: Do not publish third parties' personal data or materials covered by secrecy. For security vulnerabilities on the site, contact us privately.

home.hero_line: The cloud has a body. Energy, chips, mines, labor.
home.hero_sub: A map to make visible the physical infrastructure behind digital services and artificial intelligence — with a focus on Italy and Europe.
home.problem_title: Behind every prompt there is a material chain
home.problem_1_body: Cloud and AI are told as bodiless services: a prompt, a query, an account. The physical weight stays out of frame.
home.problem_2_body: Behind every request sit data centers, power plants, semiconductor fabs, and extraction sites — linked in a material supply chain.
home.problem_3_body: These infrastructures are often remote, poorly documented, and hard to discuss in public. The map is there to make them readable.
home.stats_title: Numbers from the map, not slogans
home.stats_note: A curated, evolving sample: better a few sites with sources than thousands of opaque pins.
home.actions_title: Three ways to use the tool
home.action_1_body: Isolate hyperscale, gas, mines, or fabs: see what stays in view and what disappears.
home.action_2_body: Click a site and read the links: who powers, who supplies, with what level of certainty.
home.action_3_body: Where data are enriched you find reliability, evidence, and notes on labor and impact.
home.roadmap_title: What is here and what is coming

roadmap_steps.title: Analyze and share
roadmap_steps.body: Time series, community-verified contributions, territorial comparisons, and export for journalism and research. Multi-stop «Anatomy» tour.

home.welcome_lead: It is a non-profit civic-tech project: it makes the physical infrastructure of cloud and AI visible so citizens, journalists, and communities can discuss it with more awareness.
home.welcome_mission_body: We do not sell services and do not represent a company. The goal is informed activism: sharing open tools, sources, and questions about territory, energy, and labor behind the digital.
home.welcome_disclaimer_body: The dataset is incomplete, evolving, and in places estimated or inferred. We prefer transparency (sources, reliability, notes) to false completeness. Use it as a starting point, not as official truth.

faq.q: Can I reuse or cite the project?

narrative.intro: Every time we use a cloud service, query an artificial intelligence, or simply send an email, we activate a physical chain that stretches across continents. Behind the "cloud" sit data centers that consume vast amounts of energy, powered by gas plants, solar farms, wind facilities, and nuclear plants. The servers inside them hold semiconductors made in highly specialized factories, which in turn depend on raw materials — lithium, cobalt, rare earths — mined from Australia to Chile, from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to China.
narrative.intro_2: This interactive map makes that hidden infrastructure visible, with a particular focus on Italy and Europe. It shows where the data centers that host our data are, which energy plants power them, and where the materials and components that make them possible come from. It is a tool meant for journalists, citizens, and decision-makers who want to understand the material dimension of the digital transformation.
narrative.data_caption: The map shows {dc_count} data centers, {rm_count} extraction and production sites, {ep_count} energy plants, and {conn_count} connections among these infrastructures in Europe and worldwide.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.heading: How we read the data
methodology.lead: Substrato mixes open inventories and curated corridors. This page explains what each reliability label means, who verifies the links, and which limits stay explicit.
methodology.intro: We use two distinct levels: confidence on the point (how reliable the site's existence and properties are) and certainty on the link (how well documented the relationship between two sites is). They are not the same thing. An OSM data center can have low confidence and no edges; a named PPA can have confirmed certainty even if a nearby point stays raw.

layers.title: Basemap (inventory)
layers.body: Points bulk-imported for geographic context: energy plants from the WRI Global Power Plant Database (Italy + EU ≥ 100 MW) and data centers from OpenStreetMap (telecom=data_center tag in the EU area). OSM for data centers is incomplete and uneven: many campuses are missing, some are misplaced, quality varies by country. WRI is more structured, but remains a global database with delays and import thresholds. Imported records do not claim to be a supply chain.

layers.title: Curated corridors (project thesis)
layers.body: A few sites enriched by hand (descriptions, impact, labor, sources) and connections with mandatory certainty + evidence_note. This is where the line «the cloud has a body» lives: documented energy, AI silicon, battery metals, labor contrast. We prefer fewer true arrows to many suggestive ones.

methodology.confidence_lead: Measures how reliable the point record is (identity, location, declared capacity).

confidence_levels.label: High
confidence_levels.body: Official document or primary operator statement (corporate fact sheet, annual report, PPA named on the site).

confidence_levels.label: Medium
confidence_levels.body: Journalistic source or coherent secondary report; typical of imported WRI plants and many curated records still being enriched.

confidence_levels.label: Low
confidence_levels.body: Indirect clue. Default for data centers imported from OpenStreetMap until there is secondary verification.

confidence_levels.label: Estimate
confidence_levels.body: Value modeled or estimated by the dataset author (e.g. average impact factors), always labeled as such on the card.

methodology.certainty_lead: Measures how well documented the relationship between two sites is (powers, connects, supplies, manufactures_for, trains). Every new edge requires certainty and an evidence note in Italian. Inferred edges are drawn lighter on the map.

certainty_levels.label: Confirmed
certainty_levels.body: Direct proof of the link: named PPA or supply contract, joint statement, corporate report that explicitly cites origin and destination.

certainty_levels.label: Likely
certainty_levels.body: Strong geographic or market evidence without site-to-site proof (same basin and same supplier of a known agreement; recognized ODM of a hyperscaler without the campus packing list).

certainty_levels.label: Inferred
certainty_levels.body: Transparent working hypothesis: grid proximity, same product class, energy cluster. Never presented as fact. A link to a substation named in a filing does not say which plant produced the electricity: that link is a grid connection, not a power supply.

certainty_levels.label: Disputed
certainty_levels.body: Conflicting sources or relevant public contestation of the link or project. Stays on the map with the label; it is not «resolved» quietly.

methodology.ladder_lead: The grade rises only with new evidence, not for narrative convenience.
ladder: From inferred to likely: coherent evidence is required (same operator/basin contract, documented market supply chain) and a note explaining why it is not yet confirmed.
From likely to confirmed: a named primary document is required (PPA, joint statement, report naming both parties). Without that the link stays likely or drops.
powers without a named PPA or offtake: never confirmed. A local energy asset on the same site/municipality without a named contract stays powers likely.

Grid connection (connects): confirmed when an EIA/screening/STMG names campus and substation, or when the plant is adjacent to its injection station. It does not say which plant produced electricity for a campus. connects inferred is allowed from a transmission injection node to campuses on the same grid cluster: the card must state it is not the campus connection and not an offtake (e.g. Turbigo 380 kV → Milan cluster). Inferred edges are drawn lighter on the map.
supplies / manufactures_for only if the material or product belongs to that supply chain (no lithium→chip or cobalt→logic foundry).
trains = cognitive labor (labeling, moderation, RLHF) toward a lab or footprint where the model is trained/served; confirmed only with an investigation or contract naming client and hub.
A site without an edge is valid: projects, context, inventories. We do not invent links to fill the map.
methodology.who_body: Editorial curation is by Relatronica (Substrato project): corridor selection, certainty/confidence compilation, evidence notes, and source updates. OpenStreetMap and WRI remain under their communities and licenses; we do not «certify» the entire automatic inventory. Community corrections go through Report (preferred: traceable GitHub issue) and are incorporated after human review — there is no anonymous direct write access to the published dataset.
methodology.when_body: Each curated record may have updated_at; the dataset_meta.json file reports the date of the last merge. We do not offer real-time updates. Typical cadence: when relevant PPAs or reports appear, when a report is verified, or in corridor enrichment batches. When citing, always note the date you consulted the map.

sources.title: WRI Global Power Plant Database
sources.body: Energy plants, CC BY 4.0 license. Import: all plants in Italy + EU ≥ 100 MW. More rigorous than OSM on structure and capacity, but not an offtake toward data centers.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap (Overpass)
sources.body: Data centers via telecom=data_center tag, ODbL license. Low confidence by default. Incomplete and uneven: useful as a basemap, insufficient alone for journalism on a single site without verification.

sources.title: Curated records and connections
sources.body: GeoJSON in data/curated/ and edges in connections_edges.json: descriptions, labor, impact, certainty. Always take priority over automatic candidates in case of conflict.

sources.title: Context overlays
sources.body: Power grid (OpenInfraMap), water stress (Aqueduct × HydroBASINS), submarine cables (historical extract). Off by default; they are not supply-chain links.

limits: Completeness of the European inventory of data centers or mines.
Physical electron-by-electron or wafer-by-rack traceability without a document.
Invented employment numbers: we prefer null + a note to a cosmetic 0.
Institutional certification or third-party audit of the dataset.
methodology.cite_body: Substrato (Relatronica), map consulted on YYYY-MM-DD, substrato.eu — also note the link certainty if you use a specific connection, and the primary source linked on the card when present.
